title: ARIA attributes need valid values
summary: An ARIA attribute has a value it does not accept, such as aria-pressed="yes". Use a value the specification allows.
problem: An aria-* attribute has a value outside what WAI-ARIA allows for it. For example, aria-pressed accepts true, false or mixed, not "yes". Other attributes expect an element id that exists on the page. Assistive technology may ignore the value or misreport it.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users get no state or a wrong one for the control, so they cannot tell whether a button is pressed, a menu is open or a field is required.
steps: Find the element, the attribute and the rejected value in the scan result.
Look up the attribute in the WAI-ARIA specification. Boolean-style attributes take the strings true or false, and some such as aria-pressed and aria-checked also accept mixed.
For attributes that point to other elements, such as aria-labeledby or aria-describedby, make sure each id exists on the page and is spelled exactly the same.
Set the value from your script when the state changes, using the exact strings, not yes, no, on or off.
whyItMatters: An invalid value is ignored or misread, so a control can announce the opposite of what it shows. This is a WCAG 4.1.2 Level A requirement (Name, Role, Value), the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Re-run the scan. In your browser's accessibility inspector, select the element and confirm its state matches what you see on screen, then change it and check again.
